title: Consolidate lightweight log-producer shims to emit structured JSON and propagate trace/correlation IDs
creator: Jordan Kim
description: Create and standardize lightweight producer shims for Redwood services and client SDKs that emit a consistent JSON log envelope and reliably propagate trace and correlation IDs across async boundaries. The goal is to reduce variability in log shape across languages and frameworks, make Loki/ELK label extraction simpler, and ensure every server and client request can be correlated to traces and metrics for low-latency troubleshooting.
background: We have many services with ad-hoc log formats and partial trace propagation. This causes expensive investigation time when an error spans multiple services and complicates dashboarding and alerting. Existing efforts (log schema, routing) have focused on ingestion-side transforms, but instrumenting the producers to emit consistent structured logs and carry context yields higher fidelity and reduces processing cost at the aggregator.
scope: Implement small language-specific shims for Node, Python, Go, and Java that wrap common logging libraries and emit a canonical JSON envelope.

Standardize field names: timestamp (RFC3339), level, message, service.name, env, trace.id, span.id, parent.span.id, request.id, user.id (optional), sdk.version, host, pid, thread, labels (freeform map serialized as JSON string for Loki compatibility).
Automatic propagation of trace and request correlation IDs through HTTP headers, internal RPC contexts, and background job payloads.
A fallback path that safely converts existing plaintext logs into the envelope when producers are not fully migrated (best-effort enrichment at the shim layer).
Compatibility mode flags to route logs to Loki with lightweight label hints or to an ELK stack when required by enterprise customers.
technical_design: The shim will be a tiny adapter library that sits between application code and the underlying logger. It will expose the same API shape as the native logger (e.g., logger.info/debug/error) but will attach a stable JSON envelope. Trace propagation will use the W3C traceparent header when available; otherwise the shim will generate a 64-bit random trace id and log it. For async work (background jobs, threads, goroutines), the shim will provide helpers to serialize trace/request metadata into job payloads and rehydrate context at worker boundaries. To keep Loki label cardinality under control, the shim will emit a top-level 'labels' JSON object that Vector/Fluentd can flatten into a few selected labels via config. Timestamp formatting will be RFC3339 with nanoseconds. The shim will be configurable via environment variables and a short JSON config that selects the output target (loki|elk|stdout), sample rate for debug-level payloads, and a 'safe-mode' that disables any potentially PII fields. The libraries will include unit tests asserting schema conformance and an integration test harness that replays synthetic requests to ensure trace IDs appear end-to-end across services and end up in sample traces in the tracing system.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Publish Node and Python shims to internal package repos; add instrumentation in 3 pilot services (auth, api-gateway, inference-proxy).
Phase 2: Enable collectors to parse the new envelope and map labels for Loki; update Vector/Fluentd recipes in staging to flatten 'labels' into loki labels.
Phase 3: Migrate additional services (Go/Java) and enable the fallback enrichment only for legacy services during the transition window.
Phase 4: Monitor error/trace mismatch rate and lower heuristic fallback after coverage reaches 90% across request paths.
Phase 5: Document and publish SDK examples for external customers (public SDK repos) and update onboarding guides in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Pilot services emit the canonical JSON envelope for 95% of logged request flows in staging.
End-to-end tests show trace.id present in both logs and traces for the pilot request paths.
Loki dashboards can extract a stable set of labels from the new envelope without increasing cardinality beyond 3x current baseline in staging.
Rollout knobs available (env flags/config) to switch between loki/elk targets and to disable PII fields without code changes.
Integration tests run in CI to validate schema and propagation on PRs touching the shims.
risks: Increased log payload size could raise egress and storage costs — mitigate by sampling and restricting large payload fields.
Incorrect label flattening risks high cardinality in Loki — mitigate via conservative default label list and ops monitoring.
Language-specific runtime constraints (Golang structured logger performance, Python GIL) may require micro-optimizations; benchmark early.
qa_steps: Deploy shims to staging pilot services and run a 48-hour synthetic load with error injection across request flows.
Query Loki for trace.id frequencies and compare against tracing system counts; produce mismatch report.
Validate that when safe-mode is enabled, PII fields (user.email, user.name) are not present in logs.
Run CI integration suite that sends sample logs to a local Vector instance and asserts label extraction rules produce the expected label set.
notes: Prefer minimal runtime allocations; avoid JSON re-serialization when underlying logger already supports structured output — provide passthrough adapters.
Keep the public SDK surface small; most of the heavy-lifting should be in internal packages and adapters to make adoption low-friction.
Coordinate with Security for a quick review on PII handling and KMS/secret access for any config that contains tokens.
